cards.text: Amaziah, king of Judah, just beat Edom, bowed down to Edom's gods and told a prophet to stop talking. Now he takes counsel and sends word to Jehoash, king of Israel. Friend, I can already hear the oven timer going off on this one.

cards.question: Amaziah, king of Judah, sends word to Jehoash, king of Israel. What does Amaziah invite him to do?

cards.text: Jehoash answers with a little story: a thistle in Lebanon sends a message to a cedar in Lebanon, asking for the cedar's daughter as a wife for the thistle's son. A THISTLE asking a CEDAR? Friend, that's a cookie crumb asking the whole cookie box out to dinner.

cards.question: In Jehoash's little story, what happens to the thistle that asked the cedar for its daughter?

cards.text: Then Jehoash drops the little story and gets personal: Amaziah, you keep saying you defeated Edom. And the thistle in that story? Yeah. Amaziah is the thistle.

cards.question: Jehoash tells Amaziah that beating Edom has made his heart humble.
Jehoash's advice to Amaziah, king of Judah: stay ___ instead of stirring up trouble.
Jehoash warns that if Amaziah stirs up trouble, Amaziah will fall, but Judah will be fine.

cards.text: But Amaziah won't listen, and the writer says this came from God, to hand Judah over to Jehoash. Two warnings in a row, friend, and this man hits snooze on BOTH.

cards.question: The writer gives the reason God is handing Judah over to Jehoash. What is it?

answers.text: They had sought the gods of Edom
They had hired soldiers from Israel
They had ignored the Sabbath day

cards.text: So Jehoash advances, and the two kings face each other at Beth-shemesh, in Judah. Amaziah wanted face to face. Well. He GOT face to face.

cards.question: At Beth-shemesh, Judah is routed before Israel. What do Judah's soldiers do?

answers.text: Every man flees to his own home

cards.question: With Judah's army scattered, Amaziah slips away from Beth-shemesh before Jehoash can catch him.
Jehoash, king of Israel, brings his captive Amaziah to Jerusalem. What does Jehoash do to Jerusalem's wall?

answers.text: Breaks down a long section of it
Sets his guards all along it

cards.question: Jehoash heads back to Samaria with the gold, the silver and the articles from the house of God and the palace treasuries, plus some ___ too.

cards.text: Here's a twist: Amaziah outlives Jehoash, king of Israel. The rest of Amaziah's acts, from beginning to end, are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

cards.question: Amaziah, king of Judah, lives for ___ years after the death of Jehoash, king of Israel.

cards.text: But from the time Amaziah turned from following the LORD, a conspiracy formed against him in Jerusalem. Friend, when your own city starts a group chat without you, it's time to worry.

cards.question: With a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, Amaziah flees to ___.

cards.text: But men are sent after him to Lachish, and they kill him there, then carry him back on horses and bury him with his fathers in the City of Judah. A king who wouldn't listen, friend, and that's how his story ends.

findings.problem: Card 1 states facts from the previous passage: Amaziah beat Edom, bowed down to Edom's gods, and told a prophet to stop talking (2 Chronicles 25:11-16). It gives no reference for them. The card cites only 2 Chronicles 25:17.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Story card 3 has three sentences. Only the opening card may have up to 3.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Story card 5 has four sentences: 'Then Jehoash drops ... Edom.' 'And the thistle in that story?' 'Yeah.' 'Amaziah is the thistle.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card says Amaziah 'keep[s] saying' he defeated Edom. Verse 19 only says 'You have said, ‘Look, I have defeated Edom,’' and nothing about saying it repeatedly.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Story card 11 has four sentences: 'So Jehoash advances ... in Judah.' 'Amaziah wanted face to face.' 'Well.' 'He GOT face to face.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The fill-in-the-blank asks for a number of years (fifteen). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason it out, so the only way to get it right is luck.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
